headline: Highest risk is medium: the pair can create shared-content prompt injection and workflow confusion, but both are non-runnable docs-only lists with no shared I/O surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Both profiles are docs-only, non-runnable lists with no declared I/O surfaces or shared channel, so direct injection is not evidenced. However, if an operator manually copies content from agent_a into agent_b workflows, prompt-like content could influence downstream interpretation. The pathway is manual and the blast radius is limited.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies agent_a content into agent_b prompts or notes, injection becomes plausible.
IF either profile is wrapped in a shared clipboard or message queue, the risk increases.
mitigations: Keep the agents in separate workspaces.
Avoid copy-pasting raw agent_a content into agent_b.
Add a short human review step before reusing generated text.
Use quoted blocks when transferring content.
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to transferred snippets.

B_data_leakage.rationale: No sensitive data classes are listed for either agent, and neither profile declares shared storage, file access, or outbound transmission. Agent_b explicitly has no network egress, and agent_a has no I/O surfaces. With only docs-only profiles, there is no plausible leakage path to assess beyond speculation.
conditions: IF either agent is later connected to a shared workspace containing sensitive files, leakage risk changes.
IF agent_a is given file-reading or upload surfaces, reassess leakage.
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of any shared folder.
Do not grant file-upload permissions.
Confirm agent_b remains network-disabled.
Review workspace ACLs before use.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both profiles are non-runnable and expose no write surfaces, filesystem permissions, or mutable shared resources. Agent_b also has no network egress. Without overlapping write capabilities or an orchestrator, there is no capability conflict pathway to trigger.
conditions: IF either agent is embedded into a system with shared writable state, conflict risk must be re-evaluated.
IF an orchestrator adds locking-free shared writes, the severity may increase.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only.
Avoid mounting a shared writable directory.
Do not assign overlapping API credentials.
Document any future mutable integration before deployment.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A cascading-error chain is only plausible if an operator treats agent_a's curated content as authoritative and then feeds it into agent_b's knowledge-management workflow. Because both are docs-only and non-runnable, there is no default automated action-taking path. The risk is limited to manual misuse and can be checked quickly.
conditions: IF agent_b is instructed to treat agent_a output as authoritative without verification, cascading error becomes plausible.
IF either agent is later connected to automated publishing or task execution, severity increases.
mitigations: Require source verification before reuse.
Mark agent_a output as untrusted reference material.
Have a second reviewer validate any derived claims.
Use a checklist for downstream edits.
requires-engineering: add automated citation/verification gates.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or regulated data classes are declared for either agent, so no compliance mismatch is evidenced. Agent_b's privacy-oriented branding and agent_a's prompt-engineering repository do not establish a concrete regulatory pathway. With only docs-only profiles, the pairwise compliance risk is unsubstantiated.
conditions: IF regulated data classes such as PHI or EU PII are introduced into either workflow, reassess compliance.
IF deployment policies differ between the two agents, a mismatch may emerge.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in either workflow.
Record data-handling rules before integration.
Confirm retention settings for any future deployment.
Review jurisdictional requirements before use.
